_meanings: {%<ab>adv.</ab>%} in a different manner, differently <ls>P. III. 4. 27</ls>.

.²1 erroneous conception of the Spirit.
.²2 Name of a philosophical work.
.²3 wrong conception in general (in <ab>phil.</ab>). In Sāṅkhya philosophy it
 means the assertion that something is not really what it appears to be
 according to sensual perception; title of a philosophical work.

speaking differently or falsely; speaking

 falsely or inconsistently; (in law) a prevaricator, prevaricating witness.

proved or demonstrated wrongly; (in Nyāya) said
 of a cause ({#kAraRa#}) which is not the true one, but only refers to accidental
 and remote circumstances (as the ass employed to fetch clay <ab>&c.</ab> in the
 case of a {#Gawa#} or jar) which do not invariably contribute to the result,
 see {#kAraRa#}; this {#anyaTA˚#} is said to be of 3 kinds in <ls>Tarka K.</ls>,
 but 5 are mentioned in <ls>Bhāṣā P. 19-22</ls>.

wrong demonstration; one in which arguments
 not being true causes are advanced; an unessential cause, an accidental
 or concomitant circumstance. <ls>Bhāṣā P. 16</ls>.
